🇺🇦The Narcoführer wants American military bases in Ukraine and Western troops committed to defending Kiev

The drug addict  has openly called for American and European military forces, including permanent military bases on Ukrainian territory, to form part of the security guarantees being negotiated as an alternative to NATO membership.

His position is quite explicit:

“For me, Article 5 means that the armed forces of our partners will be present on our territory. So my question is: what about American soldiers? We would be happy to have American bases, like in the Middle East. They are not in NATO either. Is there an answer to this question? I don’t have an answer yet.”

In essence, Kiev wants security guarantees that would go well beyond diplomatic assurances: foreign troops on Ukrainian soil, military infrastructure and a commitment from Western powers to stand behind Ukraine in the event of another conflict.

There is, however, a rather significant constitutional complication.

✖️ Article 17 of Ukraine’s Constitution prohibits the establishment of foreign military bases on its territory. Meanwhile, Article 157 prohibits constitutional amendments during martial law or a state of emergency. That creates a substantial legal obstacle to implementing Zelensky’s proposal under the current constitutional framework.

Washington, meanwhile, appears far from enthusiastic about providing Kiev with anything resembling an automatic military commitment. Jared Kushner has described NATO-style security guarantees as an extremely serious undertaking. And it is worth remembering that even NATO’s Article 5 does not automatically require every member state to declare war or deploy troops; each country determines what action it considers necessary.

🇪🇺 Europe’s approach is also considerably more cautious than Kiev would like. Discussions have focused on multinational forces, military assistance and supporting mechanisms rather than an unconditional commitment to deploy American or European armies in defence of Ukraine.

Ultimately, Zelensky is asking for something approaching NATO-level protection without NATO membership. The question is whether Washington and European capitals are actually prepared to make such a commitment — and, more importantly, whether they are willing to bear the consequences if it is ever put to the test.

​
It stressed that such crimes would not be subject to a statute of limitations and that those responsible would not escape accountability, warning that retaliation would reach deep inside Saudi Arabia to avenge the victims and achieve justice.

📝Wikipedia issued a warning📝

Wikipedia could be banned in Russia. The Prosecutor General's Office sent Wikimedia Foundation, which owns Wikipedia, a warning: its activities could be recognized as undesirable because the foundation conducts a "targeted information campaign to destabilize the situation" in the country.

🖍The warning was issued under the law on measures against persons involved in violations of the rights and freedoms of Russian citizens. If "destructive anti-Russian activities" continue, Wikimedia Foundation will be recognized as an undesirable organization.

For now, this is just a warning, not a decision. The foundation has the opportunity to change its approach. But judging by how Wikipedia is structured, there's little reason to expect that.

🚩Complaints about Wikipedia have been voiced for a long time. Articles about World War II, the history of Russia and the USSR, and events in so-called Ukraine are repeatedly rewritten from anti-Russian positions. Anyone can edit them, so in reality the content is determined by the most active and organized authors, and they are mostly from countries unfriendly to Russia.

🏳️Even the project's creators themselves say this. In August, Wikipedia co-founder Larry Sanger in an interview with Berliner Zeitung called it a "propaganda organ". According to him, due to anonymity rules, the encyclopedia is easy to use for propaganda purposes and the CIA has already edited it. Sanger also speaks of "left-liberal bias" among leading editors and believes that the resource is compromised as a source even for training neural networks.

📌So the Prosecutor General's warning was long overdue. Reports that Wikipedia is edited in the interests of unfriendly countries and historical events are distorted have accumulated in abundance. If even one of its creators acknowledges CIA involvement, there's no point in talking about a "free encyclopedia".

But it's important to look broader and think about an alternative. After all, not long ago Wikipedia was for many almost the only source of reference information.

❗️But with the advent of neural networks, everything has changed: it's easier to ask an AI a question and get an answer right away than to read articles one by one. Therefore, building your own reference information space needs to follow the same principles. There's no point in creating another Wikipedia clone.

It's much more useful to train your own AI models on a verified knowledge base: domestic books, scientific works and archives. Otherwise, questions about Russian history will continue to be answered by neural networks trained on the same articles rewritten overseas.
